text: ok nice. now another one for ya, and this one might take some elbow grease, but hop back to the world editor with me and notice we have layer control, ground, level 1 level 2 etc. well, lets say i place some walls and floors on like level 2 or 3, and then i want to come back and edit the interior of level 1, effectively im shit out of luck because i cant hide the floors above me, so i just see effectively nothing for the floor im placing on, so there needs to be effectively a default for this behavior, show me the floor im on, and then also let me disable the walls for my same floor, so i can place props correctly without needing to build everything from this extremely specific one way, as it stands to do anything like make a building, i would need to: place ground -> place props -> place stairs -> place walls -> go up a floor -> repeat and stepping out of that order at all would make it so the entire floor is fucked

events.text: Built the Sims-style storey cutaway as the DEFAULT world-editor view: visibleStoreyPieces (world/pieces.ts) hides every piece on storeys above the active floor (floors below stay as context), and a WALLS Up/Down pill next to the floor control additionally hides the active floor's walls for interior/prop editing. WorldEditorSurface derives the visible list from the full authored list per floor/walls change and hands the viewport only that, so live overlay, picking, and selection agree with the screen; the full list stays authoritative for placements. New EditorState.wallsDown + action-bar toggle per the FLOORCTL home. Commit 1eedda256, hot-reloads — verify: place floors on Ground and Level 2, drop to Level 1: Level 2 pieces vanish; toggle WALLS Down on a floor with walls: they hide.
